title: The thrill of Basie's band and Basie as leader
summary: Edison calls the Basie band the greatest thrill of his life and praises Basie's humor and respect for soloists.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: And, gee whiz, what a thrill it was to play with that band. That was the greatest thrill of my life, being a member of Count Basie's aggregation.
At that time. It was -- well, now it's a thrill to be with him. But that time, oh.
Yeah. But I mean, that was the impact of it.

Stanley, we couldn't wait to get on the bandstand at night. It was just like a horse prancing to get out on the racetrack. We were just nervous if we weren't on the bandstand. That was just such a thrill. It was absolutely -- I don't think nobody on earth is a better bandleader than Count Basie.
Now, explain that. In what way was he --
In anyway. He was a very humorous guy. He was easy to get along with and he knows how to handle men and he knew that the soloists were important in his band. So

he didn't try to make an ensemble band out of it, he still kept it a solo band. He loved players, he loved to hear them play, he liked to hear Herschel play, he liked to hear everybody play in his band. That's the reason why he let you play, you know. He loved to hear Buck play, he liked to hear me play, he liked to hear Jo Jones. And he's the greatest for stomping off the tempo. I've never, never heard Basie -- we've never started out, on the introduction of any tune -- no tune, unless it was the right tempo. He noodles around on the piano --
